common_name: Hot Rocks Dark Leaf Red Sedum (Dark-Foliage Red-Flowered Stonecrop)
scientific_name: Sedum telephium 'Hot Rocks Dark Leaf Red'

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated starts in spring in well-drained soil; this 2026 Syngenta Flowers introduction was bred for heavier branching and reduced lodging compared with open-market stonecrops.

directions: This compact stonecrop pairs near-black chocolate foliage with clusters of vivid deep red flowers that hold through the season rather than fading. Breeders selected it for tighter, sturdier branching than typical garden-center sedums, which keeps the clumps upright and reduces the flopping and splitting older varieties are prone to. It also shows notably better resistance to powdery mildew, a common problem on sedum foliage late in summer. Give it full sun and well-drained soil with minimal supplemental water once established, as for any stonecrop.
sources: Syngenta Flowers (syngentaflowers.com) — Hot Rocks Dark Leaf Red Sedum, California Spring Trials 2026 coverage

common_name: iCandy XL Deep Yellow Begonia (Large-Flowered Dark-Foliage Interspecific Begonia)
scientific_name: Begonia x hybrida 'iCandy XL Deep Yellow'

planting.note: Transplant vegetatively propagated starts after frost danger passes; this higher-vigor XL selection in Syngenta's 2026 iCandy line is sized for quart pots and larger hanging baskets rather than smaller packs.

directions: iCandy XL Deep Yellow is an interspecific hybrid begonia with a mounding, cascading form, its deep yellow double flowers set sharply against near-black chocolate-colored foliage. It was bred for heavier branching and greater vigor than the standard iCandy series colors, making it a better fit for quart containers and larger hanging baskets rather than small packs. The plant performs in part sun to shade, which makes it a flexible choice for porch and patio displays that do not get strong direct afternoon sun. Keep soil evenly moist and feed regularly to sustain its heavy, continuous bloom.
sources: Syngenta Flowers (syngentaflowers.com) — iCandy XL Deep Yellow Begonia, California Spring Trials 2026 coverage

common_name: Coffee Shop Lavender Latte Dahlia (Dark-Foliage Double-Flowered Patio Dahlia)
scientific_name: Dahlia x hybrida 'Coffee Shop Lavender Latte'

planting.note: Transplant vegetatively propagated starts after frost danger passes into well-drained, fertile soil; part of Syngenta's 2026 Coffee Shop dahlia line bred for coffee-dark foliage and strong garden performance.

directions: Lavender Latte carries fully double lavender-toned blooms that hold their form well, set off by distinctive coffee-dark foliage that gives the plant garden interest even between flushes of bloom. Its upright habit with medium vigor and strong stems keeps the display tidy without much staking, and Syngenta notes excellent resistance to powdery mildew compared with older patio dahlia types. It is suited to patio pots, cutting gardens, and landscape beds, blooming continuously through the season in full to part sun. Grow in fertile, well-drained soil with regular moisture for best flower production.
sources: Syngenta Flowers (syngentaflowers.com) — Coffee Shop Lavender Latte Dahlia product page

common_name: Pretty Little White Splash Geranium (Compact Bicolor Interspecific Pelargonium)

planting.note: Transplant vegetatively propagated starts after frost danger passes; introduced in 2026 as the first true companion color to Pretty Little Pink Splash in Syngenta's interspecific geranium series.

directions: White Splash is a naturally compact, early-flowering interspecific geranium with a bold red eye visible from a distance, its petals white toward the outer edge and dark pink toward the center. It was launched as the companion color to the existing Pretty Little Pink Splash, extending the series' bicolor look into a cooler palette. Enhanced branching and multi-bloom flowering give it full coverage even in small pots, making it well suited to compact container programs. Grow in full sun with regular moisture and feeding for continuous bloom through the season.
sources: Syngenta Flowers (syngentaflowers.com) — Pretty Little geranium series, CAST 2026 coverage

common_name: Zydeco Gold Zinnia (Fully Double Gold-Orange Interspecific Zinnia)

planting.note: Start indoors and transplant, or direct sow, after the last frost once soil is warm; a 2026 addition to Syngenta's interspecific Zydeco zinnia series bred for disease resistance.

directions: Zydeco Gold bears fully double, golden-orange blooms on a vigorously branched plant, with the dense petal count extending the display life of each flower compared with single-flowered zinnias. It carries the Zydeco series' interspecific disease resistance, giving it a cleaner look through heat and humidity than many older zinnia types, alongside good heat and drought tolerance. Its adaptable branching habit works equally well in cell packs, premium pots, or mixed baskets. Plant in full sun with good air circulation and well-drained soil for the strongest season-long performance.
sources: Syngenta Flowers (syngentaflowers.com) — Zydeco Gold Zinnia, California Spring Trials 2026 coverage

common_name: Scent Mini Blue Lavender (Compact First-Year-Flowering English Lavender)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated starts in spring in well-drained soil; a more compact, first-year-flowering companion to Syngenta's original Scent Blue lavender, introduced for 2026.

directions: Scent Mini Blue is a next-generation selection in Syngenta's Scent lavender line, matching the original Scent Blue for fill and flowering timing in its first year but finishing about a third more compact. Silvery-green foliage mounds into a vigorously branched plant topped with deep purple-and-white flower spikes prized for fragrance. Its smaller finished size makes it easier to program in quart pots and smaller formats while still meeting typical spring sale timing. Grow in full sun with well-drained soil and minimal supplemental watering once established, as for other English lavenders.
sources: Syngenta Flowers (syngentaflowers.com) — Scent Mini Blue Lavandula angustifolia product page
